stem:
Fluorine-18 (¹⁸₉F) is a radioactive nuclide that is used as a tracer in positron emission tomography (PET scanning). Fluorine-18 decays to a nuclide of oxygen (O) according to

¹⁸₉F → $^{P}_{Q}\mathrm{X}$ + $^{R}_{8}\mathrm{O}$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by a tracer.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the symbol of the particle that is represented by X and the values of P, Q and R.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain how the radioactive decay of fluorine-18 results in the emission from the body of the gamma-ray photons that are detected during a PET scan.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how the detection of the gamma-ray photons is used to produce an image of the tissue being examined.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The half-life of fluorine-18 is *T*.
A patient is injected with amount of substance *n* of fluorine-18.
parts.text: Determine an expression for the initial value *R*₀ of the rate *R* of production of gamma-ray photons by the tracer, in terms of *n*, *T* and the Avogadro constant *N*ₐ.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On [[fig:f1]], sketch the variation with time *t* of *R*.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: A blank graph grid with vertical axis R, marked R₀ at the top and 0 at the origin, and horizontal axis t, marked 0 at the origin and T at a tick.
